newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica money mkt shortage at highest since May 6.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica money mkt shortage at highest since May 6.

text.p: The money market shortage surged to 9.208 billion rand on Wednesday -- its highest level in nearly four months, Reserve Bank figures released on Thursday show.
Dealers said the shortage, which was up about 500 million rand from Tuesday's 8.705 billion rand, was just below the 9.357 billion registered on May 6.
But the increase had not come as a surprise.
"It's normal month-end flows, government salaries and so on," a dealer said.
The shortage was expected to continue rising throughout the week, possibly to above the 10 billion rand mark "for one or two days", another trader said.
"But we expect to see it come off quite rapidly in September," he said.
Short-term money market rates also continued to ease amid good institutional and offshore demand in the three- to twelve-month area.

Various banks quoted the 90-day BA rate at between 15.90 and 16.05 percent from 16.00 to 16.10 percent on Tuesday, while three-month NCDs were also lower at between 16.50 and 16.65 percent from 16.55 and 16.70 percent on Tuesday.
"We are seeing good demand in the market for shorter assets," a dealer said. "There seems to be a little more positive sentiment around."
Another trader said a growing perception that Bank rate -- currently at 16 percent -- would not be hiked was also helping short-term rates lower.
"After the market discounted a rate hike, it now seems there is not going to be one (rate hike) and the rates are coming lower," he said.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Tuesday he did not see an immediate need for a Bank rate hike despite pressure in the banking system.
Dealers said that they would look to the three-month Treasury Bill tender rate on Friday for further signs of rate hike prospects being reduced.
"If the rate continues to trend down it is going to signal a move away from a rate hike for now," one said.
The three-month Treasury Bill rate fell to 16.09 percent last Friday from 16.19 percent the week before.
